title: Player Of The Year
protagonist: Renata Voss, Chair of the AVCA Player Of The Year Committee
primary_metric: the gap, in composite z-score points and as a percent gap, between the #1- and #2-ranked finalist under each committee member's proposed methodology

options.A: Adopt Marcus's All-Purpose Production Index -- a position-blind, unweighted average z-score across Kills/Set, Aces/Set, Blocks/Set, Assists/Set, and Digs/Set. Names Anna Stevenson (MB, Louisville) Player Of The Year.
options.B: Adopt Diane's Role-Weighted x Team-Success Composite -- position-specific z-scores multiplied by a team-success factor tied to the finalist's team's final RPI rank. Names Sydney Hilley (S, Wisconsin) Player Of The Year.

legacy_conversion_note: Original source (source/Y2/Session 5/Player Of The Year) posed a 14-way, fully open 'pick one finalist' dilemma with no stated methodology -- not strictly binary, so this case sat at the concepting stage until the human-approved lock in cases/_concepts/LEGACY_DILEMMA_LOCKS_2026-08-20.md reframed it as a binary methodology choice (which of two committee members' scoring systems the committee adopts), each formula applied end-to-end across all 14 real finalists rather than the source's own open pick. Both formulas, the national reference population, and every finalist's computed score under both systems come directly from cases/_concepts/research_notes/player-of-the-year-analytics_2026-08-20.md, a prior research pass that extracted the full 9-tab statistics workbook via script (not hand-computed) and cross-checked every cell. No number in this case was invented for the conversion -- every per-set stat, RPI rank, and W-L record in Appendix A is real 2027-2028 NCAA Division I data from the provided workbook, and every z-score/composite figure in the research notes and this case's balance object is a mechanical, reproducible function of those real inputs plus the two disclosed formulas.

deliverables.text: A completed Methodology A composite table for all 14 finalists: each finalist's z-score in all five production categories (scoring unranked categories at z=0) and her final average CompositeA score.
A completed Methodology B composite table for all 14 finalists: role-relevant category z-scores, RoleZ average, TeamMult from the RPI formula, and final CompositeB score.
A force ranking of all 14 finalists, 1 through 14, under each methodology, side by side.
At least two original visual displays comparing the two methodologies' composite scores or rankings.
A written comparison of the margin (composite points and percent gap) between the #1- and #2-ranked finalist under each methodology.

appendices.title: 2027-2028 AVCA First-Team All-American Finalists: Full Season Statistics
How the AVCA Selects Its Player Of The Year

balance.argument_a: Under Methodology A (position-blind), Anna Stevenson's elite .427 hitting percentage and 1.35 blocks/set (both far above the national top-300 average of 1.084) produce the single highest average z-score of any of the 14 finalists, +0.526 -- but only barely: Sydney Hilley's +0.517 average is 0.009 z-score points behind, a 1.74% relative gap. This is effectively a statistical coin flip -- Methodology A's own verdict is fragile.
balance.argument_b: Under Methodology B (role-weighted x team-success), Sydney Hilley's 11.95 assists/set is the #1 mark nationally and produces the single largest z-score of any player in the entire dataset (+2.585) once she is compared only to her own role's benchmark instead of being diluted across categories she doesn't play. Paired with Wisconsin's #2 RPI and their championship win over #1 Louisville, her composite (+3.851) leads Nicole Peterson, the #2 finalist under this system, by 0.731 points -- a 23.4% relative gap. Methodology B's verdict is decisive, not marginal.
balance.margin_basis: Both methodologies were run end-to-end (research_notes file) across the same real 14-finalist dataset. Methodology A's own top-two margin is 0.009 composite points / 1.74% relative (Stevenson +0.526 vs. Hilley +0.517). Methodology B's own top-two margin is 0.731 composite points / 23.4% relative (Hilley +3.851 vs. Peterson +3.117). margin_pct records the tighter of the two races (Methodology A's), which is the case's real balance-test number: the two methodologies don't just disagree on a winner, one produces a razor-thin verdict and the other a comfortable one.

derived.twist_note: Stevenson's Blocks/Set would only need to move from 1.35 to 1.344 (a 0.006 swing, well within ordinary box-score revision) to erase Methodology A's entire 0.009-point margin and hand the win to Hilley -- the Twist's real, defensible point (see FACILITATOR.md).

modeling_assumptions.text: Methodology A scores any category a finalist isn't nationally ranked in at league average (z=0) rather than as a penalized zero, because a missing national rank in a category reflects the player's role, not a failed attempt.

The national reference population (Appendix B) is drawn only from each stat's own national ranked leaderboard (the top 150-1,500 players), an already-elite subpopulation, not the full ~5,000-plus D-I field -- the only publicly available national ranking data.

Methodology B's team-success multiplier curve (linear decay from RPI 1 to RPI 50, capped at +50%, zero bonus beyond RPI 50) is one reasonable scenario-level implementation of 'weigh the quality of the teams,' not a universal formula.

sensitivity_note: Both MA1's z=0 convention and MA3's TeamMult curve are load-bearing to which methodology looks more defensible. Flex either by +/-50% (per SPEC's standard sensitivity test) and re-check whether Methodology A's razor-thin 1.74% margin or Methodology B's comfortable 23.4% margin moves, and by how much -- see FACILITATOR.md for the facilitator-only analysis.

cohort_bands.note: Runs as written. Split the room into a Marcus camp and a Diane camp for the 10:00-15:00 pressure-test; each camp defends its methodology using its own D1/D2/D3 tables before the twist drops.

Instead of two full camps, pair students so every pair has computed both methodologies for at least 3 finalists each; the 20:00-30:00 deep-conflict block drops to a single thread (fragility of Methodology A's 1.74% margin vs. the modeling choices baked into Methodology B's multiplier).

No vote to take. Anchor 1 becomes a stated initial lean (which methodology feels more defensible before computing anything). The facilitator plays the other committee member directly, pushing back with the real numbers. The twist still lands (see FACILITATOR.md); 'who reverses' becomes 'would you reverse, and why.'
